body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-30 on PR #2028 at head a5332b7668.

`scripts/lib/pr-lifecycle.sh` decides CI is terminal-green with:

    if [ "$check_count" -gt 0 ] && [ "$pending_count" -eq 0 ]; then terminal_green=1

It counts rollup entries. It never asserts that the repo ruleset's REQUIRED
checks - `validate-author`, `Fast Tests (Smoke + Unit)`, `Test Suite Summary` -
are among them.

The failure mode is a partially-registered rollup, which is the normal state for
the first ~30s after a push: the cheap workflows (`validate-author`,
`Classify image work`, `evaluate`) register and complete quickly, while the
`Test Suite` workflow is still queueing. At that instant check_count=8 and
pending_count=0, so the predicate holds and the harness emits
PR_LIFECYCLE_STATUS=green. Measured: the run for a5332b7668 was still
`status=pending` at the moment the harness printed green, and the eight graded
checks contained none of the three required ones.

The script's own comment shows the race was known - "gh pr checks --watch ...
can return while the rollup still contains pending checks" - but the guard
written for it (`ever_registered`, "absence is not green") only covers a
COMPLETELY empty rollup. A rollup that is non-empty and non-pending yet missing
every required check passes.

Why this matters beyond a wrong status string: the merge path is
`gh pr merge --squash --admin`, and `--admin` bypasses branch protection, so
GitHub's own required-status-check enforcement is not a backstop either. Both
safety nets miss the same case, so a `--merge` submit landing in this window
would merge code whose test suite never ran. This did not happen here only
because the gate carried authorize_merge=false.

Suggested fix: grade against the required check NAMES, not a count. Resolve them
from the ruleset (or pin them in the script) and require each to be present with
a SUCCESS conclusion before terminal_green. Absence of a required check should
be its own non-green status, distinct from ci-not-registered.
title: pr-lifecycle grades a head green when the required checks never registered - it counts checks, not their identities
